 Hon'Ble Jitendra Kumar Sinha, J. 
1. Heard Sri Rajeev Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Shiv Dutt Shukla,
learned A.G.A. appearing for the State respondents and perused the record.

2. Present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 0210 of 2022,
under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 Ipc, Police Station Bahariya, District Prayagraj with the
prayer that in the event of arrest, applicants may be released on bail.
3.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and they have an apprehension that they may be arrested in the above-mentioned case.

He further submits that no offence is made out against the applicants as the applicants are the marginal witnesses of the alleged Will which has been prepared fraudulently by the co-accused Narendra Kumar.
It is submitted that the applicants are not beneficiary of the alleged Will deed.

It is further submitted that co-accused Narendra Kumar has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 10.10.2025 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 482 BNSS No. 7963 of 2025.
It is further submitted that the applicants are having criminal history of one case, which has been explained in the memo of application.
It is also submitted that applicants undertake to cooperate during trial and they would appear as and when required by the investigating agency or Court.

It is lastly submitted that in case applicants are granted anticipatory bail, they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and they will cooperate with the investigation and would obey all conditions of bail.
4.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has opposed the application for anticipatory bail and submitted that the applicant has filed an application u/482 for quashing the FIR, which is pending before this Court.
5. I have considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.

6. Co-accused Narendra Kumar who is said to have prepared alleged Will deed fradulently has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 10.10.2025 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 482 BNSS No. 7963 of 2025.
The applicants are having criminal history of one case, which has been explained in the memo of application.
The applicants are said to to be marginal witnesses of the said Will deed.

7. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, the Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

sentences.text: The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

10. In the event of arrest of the applicants- Rajesh Pratap Singh and Chhedi Lal involved in the aforesaid case crime, they shall be released on anticipatory bail on their furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned,
with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicants shall not tamper with evidence and that they would appear before the trial Court on the date fixed unless exempted by the Court concerned;
(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her/them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) The applicants would cooperate during trial and would not misuse the liberty of bail.
(iv) The applicants shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court concerned.
11.
In default of any of the conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicants herein.

(Jitendra Kumar Sinha,J.) November 7, 2025 Abhishek  Rajesh Pratap Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135835322/
